passage:
allocate — 分配；配置
Last spring, a small city museum invited two researchers to study how visitors allocate attention.

artifact — 人工制品；文物
'When a label offers a story,' Ortiz explained, 'visitors treat the object as a character rather than an artifact.'

overwhelming — 令人感到压倒的；巨大的
He suggests that large artworks can feel overwhelming, whereas small objects invite close looking.

lingered — 逗留；徘徊
A few tourists lingered in the local history gallery for over an hour, reading every label.

fascinating — 极有趣的；迷人的
'A familiar object can be boring to one person and fascinating to another.' The researchers concluded that museums should offer different kinds of labels: some with stories, some with facts, and some with questions.

limitation — 限制；局限
Despite this limitation, the museum decided to use the findings.

initially — 最初；起初
The director, who initially doubted the project, now calls it 'the most useful study we have ever done'.

revealed — 揭示；显示
The study also revealed a practical problem.
